question: What native context-pressure behavior should OpenClaw own for saturated child or sub-agent sessions?
rationale: Current code exposes parent linkage and context usage, but maintainers still need to choose the threshold semantics, parent/operator notification target, and whether recovery is observe-only, parent-routed, or automatic.

options.title: Define a narrow diagnostics signal first
options.body: Add a context-pressure classification and notification path for saturated child sessions, then require live proof before adding automatic rerouting or recovery.

options.title: Add configurable parent recovery policy
options.body: Introduce explicit threshold and parent/recovery configuration, accepting a larger user-facing API and upgrade surface.

options.title: Keep this as external fleet monitoring
options.body: Leave OpenClaw core as reporting-only and document that fleet-specific saturation recovery belongs to external orchestration for now.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow diagnostics signal first
recommendation.body: Add a context-pressure classification and notification path for saturated child sessions, then require live proof before adding automatic rerouting or recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a product-scope choice about how far core should go into parent-orchestrator recovery, and this is the best available routing candidate from the inspected ownership signals.
